body:
Confirming the same failure class on Godot 4.5.stable.official (876b290332ec6f2e6d173d08162a02aa7e6ca46d), official Linux x86_64 build (sha256 cd8bb15130f92aad58a4e9fdd10117172b14c703edec8819c97ec6cdd45691b8), Debian 12 / headless, so this is not macOS/MoltenVK-specific.

Two variants, both exit code 132, both before the main scene is instantiated:

1. `user://` cannot be created (XDG_DATA_HOME whose parent is a regular file): three ERROR lines (`ensure_user_data_dir` at core/os/os.cpp:418, `Could not create directory: 'user://logs'`) and then the crash.
2. The user data dir exists but `logs` is a regular file: **not a single ERROR line reaches stderr**, only the crash banner plus `ERROR: FATAL: Index p_index = 1 is out of bounds (size() = 0). at: get (./core/templates/cowdata.h:187)`.

Reproduced with a project containing no game code (one empty `Node` as main scene), and it also happens with `--quit-after 0`, i.e. before the main loop. `godot --headless --path <min-project> --log-file /nonexistent-dir/foo.log --quit-after 5` crashes identically. Setting `debug/file_logging/enable_file_logging.pc=false` makes both variants exit 0 — which points at the file logger creation; we cannot name the frame ourselves because the official binary has no debug symbols and `--verbose` produces no frames after "Dumping the backtrace."

No backtrace is possible for us, so I cannot prove this is the same root cause as here, but the trigger (unwritable log target) and the "no readable error" symptom match exactly.

Could this be backported to the 4.5 branch as well? The 4.5 line appears to have no cherry-pick of #121926, and read-only/blocked user-data directories are a real support case on Windows (AV/EDR, roaming profile policy).
